tasks.latestTerminalSummary:
Card A's identities are correct, with one sign error in its update rule. Its machinery (state, update and labels) is the known continued-fraction/SQUFOF principal-cycle machinery. No end-to-end bound is earned, and verified improvement stays **NONE**.

I froze the brief and all nine inputs before starting, and none of them changed during the review. I preregistered one fixed exact certificate, on Gower–Wagstaff's own example N=22117019 plus six tiny moduli. All 16 checks passed with no failures. I added one extra structural check afterwards; it is labelled post-hoc in the report and also passed. There was no timing, sweep or search over N.

**Checked identities**
- **Raw recurrence:** correct, including the size bound b < 2√(Na)+a. Its step depends on the integer value, not on a mod p, so a Pollard-rho-style collision modulo an unknown factor doesn't carry forward. States quickly reach the size of N.
- **Divided-norm update:** the identity is correct and the division is exact.
- **Sign error:** a reduced state already has P just below √N, so Card A's rule "pick P' = P + kb near √N" always picks k=0. That gives c=a, the trivial reverse edge, on every reduced state. The forward step needs P' ≈ −√N, which is exactly the continued-fraction step P_{n+1} = q·Q_n − P_n.
- **Reverse edges:** label products are exactly +1 (P'=P) and −1 (P'=−P).
- **No branching:** every reduced form has exactly one reduced neighbour on each side. A non-backtracking walk is therefore forced to be the deterministic principal cycle, so "mixing of non-backtracking walks" has nothing to act on.

**Known-method mapping**
- The state (a,P,b) is the quadratic form (a,2P,b) of discriminant 4N, i.e. Gower–Wagstaff's principal-cycle form. The certificate reproduces rows 1–18 of their Table 1.
- The product of edge labels equals ±A_n mod N, the continued-fraction convergent numerator. So a "labelled residual" is the CFRAC relation A_n² ≡ (−1)ⁿQ_n with Q_n left unfactored.
- A coefficient collision is a two-term CFRAC dependency. SQUFOF's queue test (their Prop. 3.2) already compares coefficients this way, but only to spot trivial square roots, not as the factoring event. I found no source stating the "pure collision on one cycle" variant, but it is a degenerate case of CFRAC relation combination, so no novelty is supported.

**What a collision can output.** I proved a small lemma (Hilbert 90 plus ramification at the primes of N) that sorts collisions into three types:
- **Same form:** impossible within one period.
- **Conjugate:** this covers every prime-power |a|. These carry at most one bit, the same one the classical half-period method gives. All 400 in the certificate were trivial.
- **Mixed:** these need |a| to have at least two distinct primes not dividing 4N. Whether one splits N is the same ambiguous-class question SQUFOF faces, and that is a heuristic. In the certificate, 56 of 92 split N; that is one cycle, not probability evidence.

**Stopping and cost**
- **Stopping rule:** stop at a proper gcd, at gcd(a,N)>1, or when Q_n=1 returns (failure for this multiplier). When u ≢ ±1, gcd(u−1,N) is always proper.
- **Scope:** the lemma covers odd primes dividing N exactly once. Odd prime powers can never give a nontrivial collision.
- **Cost:** only a heuristic, about N^{1/4} steps and N^{1/4} stored coefficients. That is the same order as SQUFOF's heuristic, with worse memory.

**Rejection-sampling cost.** Accepted, extended to every root multiplicity. Each unit square has r = 2^(number of odd primes)·c₂ roots (c₂ = 1, 2 or 4 depending on the power of 2 in N). Acceptance is rM/φ, a collision is useful with probability 1−2/r, and the cheapest cost is about √(φ/r). This only covers that one uniform sampler. Plain random gcd already succeeds at the same √N scale, and continued fractions show what structured acquisition gains.

**Missing computation and repair**
- **Missing:** a paid way to produce collisions that split N (the "mixed" kind above) for less than the roughly N^{1/4} birthday on cycle coefficients.
- **Repair:** move to the imaginary quadratic class group. Each class there has a unique reduced form, so collisions are exact, and small prime forms give genuine branching. Inputs are paid in polynomial time, and an element of order 2 gives a factor. This is Shanks' class-group method (Schoof, about N^{1/5} under GRH), so it gives no gain. I did not read those sources.

Everything is in `research/findings/`; open `W013-residual-cycle-review.md` first. The 19 artifacts include the certificate, its output and the post-hoc check, and the source PDF and text are under `-source/`. All are hashed in `W013-residual-cycle-review-delivery.sha256`, which verifies.
